title: The World of AI: Legal Models catalogue of open legal AI models
answer: The World of AI publishes a Legal Models page that catalogues the 1000 most-downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. The data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, and every model links to its own Hub page. The most useful thing it offers is a daily snapshot of which open models tuned for legal text are most downloaded, though the supplied text does not list the models themselves.

sections.body: The World of AI publishes this page as part of its AI ecosystem section on technology and core infrastructure. It is a catalogue page for Legal Models, not a report or article. Its stated scope is the 1000 most-downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. The page says the data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, and that every model links to its own Hub page. It was last verified on 2026-09-29. The page also carries promotional notes about books, consulting services, audits, and a novel, so it mixes catalogue information with commercial material.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page says the Legal Models section tracks the 1000 most-downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub. Each entry is meant to show licence, downloads, and release date, and the list is refreshed daily. The data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, and every model links to its own Hub page. The page also describes a site search covering the full text of every published page, all built from the same database. That database includes state AI laws, a lawsuit tracker, a glossary, a tools directory, AI companies, a research library, an MCP server registry, compliance frameworks, sources, people, calculators, and weekly digests. It gives a citation format and says it was last verified on 2026-09-29. It also promotes books by Stephen R. Jordan, including The Operating Discipline for AI Library series, and says SRJ Consulting & Services has published its first work of fiction on AI, The AI Lawyer, a novel, out 17 August 2026. It lists audits and services, including the AI Business Enablement Audit, the AI Readiness & Performance Assessment, the AI Risk & Governance Review, the AI Efficiency & Process Optimization, the AI IT Security Audit, and the AI IT Security Implementation & Strategy. It describes an atlas of artificial intelligence covering what the law says, who is suing whom, and what the words mean, with every page rebuilt daily from primary sources and carrying the date it was last verified.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the catalogue covers the 1000 most-downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub, refreshed daily, with licence, downloads, and release date. It says the data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, and that every model links to its own Hub page. It gives a last verified date of 2026-09-29. It also states that The AI Lawyer, a novel, is out 17 August 2026. The supplied text does not list individual model names, download counts, licence names, or release dates.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Legal can use this source as a daily updated index of open models tuned for legal text. It shows which open legal models are most downloaded on the Hugging Face Hub, and it points to licence, download, and release date fields, so it can help track the open model layer of legal AI rather than closed products. The page also says the wider site database includes a lawsuit tracker, state AI laws, a glossary, compliance frameworks, and other legal and governance material, so it can act as an entry point to those resources. Its value is mainly as a catalogue and pointer, not as analysis or legal advice.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Legal

sections.body: This is a catalogue landing page with little explanatory substance in the supplied text. It does not list the actual models, download counts, licences, or release dates, only says those fields are included. It does not explain how legal models are identified or what counts as tuned for legal text. It covers open models on the Hugging Face Hub, so it does not cover closed or proprietary legal AI systems. It is partly commercial, promoting books, consulting services, audits, and a novel. It is dated by its last verified date of 2026-09-29 and is refreshed daily, but the harvested text is a snapshot. It does not offer legal advice.
